Registered with knowledge-file-staleness-sweep.
invariants: every rule has a non-empty remediation
every claim is a real S-id in S1..S27
no numeric limit appears anywhere except this file

fire_rate_caveat: Every fire_rate below was measured on 934 expert-authored Claude CODE skills in this marketplace, NOT on novice-authored claude.ai ORGANIZATION Skills — the population this studio actually serves (S23, owner-gated). A 0.0% rate here means 'these authors already do this', never 'the check is worthless'. The rates are recorded so a reader can discount them, not so they can be cited as authority. ⛔ The corpus was 934 SKILL.md files when these rates were measured. Adding this studio's own SKILL.md in Phase 5 made it 935, so every n/934 is a DATED SNAPSHOT and is one skill behind by construction. It is deliberately NOT re-measured to chase the delta: the rates are recorded so a reader can discount a heuristic, and no decision here turns on the third decimal place. Re-measure when the sweep falls due (stale_after), not when the denominator moves by one.

rules.rule: SKILL.md begins with a YAML frontmatter block delimited by --- and it parses
rules.rationale: An unparseable frontmatter means the skill cannot be discovered at all; the failure is total and silent.
rules.remediation: Ensure the first line is `---`, the block closes with `---`, and the contents are valid YAML.

rules.rule: frontmatter carries a non-empty `name`
rules.rationale: Required field; absent means the upload is malformed.
rules.remediation: Add `name: <lowercase-hyphenated-id>` to the frontmatter.

rules.rule: `name` is at most 64 characters
rules.rationale: Documented hard limit.
rules.remediation: Shorten the name. Keep the distinctive noun or gerund and drop qualifiers.

rules.rule: `name` matches ^[a-z0-9-]+$ (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens only)
rules.rationale: Documented character class. An uppercase letter or underscore is a hard reject.
rules.remediation: Lowercase the name and replace underscores or spaces with hyphens.

rules.rule: `name` contains no XML tags
rules.rationale: Documented prohibition.
rules.remediation: Remove angle-bracket markup from the name.

rules.rule: frontmatter carries a non-empty `description`
rules.rationale: The description is the sole discovery signal (S3). Absent, the skill can never be selected.
rules.remediation: Add a `description:` stating what the skill does AND when to use it.

rules.rule: `description` is at most 1024 characters
rules.rationale: Documented hard limit.
rules.remediation: Trim to the capability plus its trigger conditions; move detail into the body.

rules.rule: `description` contains no XML tags
rules.rationale: Documented prohibition; the description is injected into a system prompt.
rules.remediation: Remove angle-bracket markup from the description.
rules.predicate_note: TAG-SHAPED ONLY: </?name .../>. S1 prohibits XML TAGS, not the characters `<` and `>`. Measured 2026-08-24 on 934 skills: a bare-angle-bracket predicate fired 63 times and inspection showed most were ASCII arrows (inquiry->apply->admit); the tag-shaped predicate fires 15 times, all genuine tags. A FAIL-tier predicate broader than its own sourced claim is a heuristic wearing a citation.

rules.rule: `name` equals the containing directory name
rules.rationale: WARN, not FAIL — DEMOTED 2026-08-24 on Anthropic's own worked example. Support article 12512198 says 'Ensure the folder name matches your skill's name', but the example on the same page pairs a skill named 'Brand Guidelines' with a folder 'my-skill/'. Byte-equality is therefore not demonstrated by the vendor, and nothing anywhere states that an upload FAILS on a mismatch. This table's own discipline says a FAIL needs ground truth that does not depend on who authored the skill; an equality rule the vendor's own example violates is not that. Anthropic's upload-error list (12512180) does name 'Skill folder name doesn't match the skill name' as a failure cause, so the two Anthropic sources CONTRADICT each other — which is precisely the condition under which this table warns rather than blocks (cf. ZP02 on root layout, ZP10 on filename case).
rules.remediation: Match them if you can — it is the safer reading of 12512180's error list. Nothing demonstrates an upload fails on a mismatch, and Anthropic's own example does not match, so this does not block.
rules.demotion_evidence: reference/platform-constraints.md#zip-root-settlement, unresolved side-issues. RE-PROMOTION TO FAIL REQUIRES NEW EVIDENCE, not a preference: an observed upload that rejects a mismatched pair. The packer is unaffected either way — it roots the archive at the DIRECTORY name, which is what Anthropic's example does.

rules.rule: the body after the frontmatter is non-empty
rules.rationale: A skill with a description and no instructions is discoverable and useless.
rules.remediation: Write the procedure the skill should follow when selected.

rules.rule: `name` is not a reserved word
rules.rationale: S1 states names may not use reserved words. The list ships EMPTY-BUT-PRESENT: the constraint is real, its contents are not published, and an empty list enforces nothing while keeping the slot honest and greppable.
rules.remediation: If an upload is rejected for a reserved name, add the rejected token to reserved_words here and record the rejection in reference/platform-constraints.md.
rules.unverified: S1 says 'no reserved words' and the claims table does not enumerate them — verified by: re-reading platform.claude.com best-practices, or an upload attempt. Routed to plan section 8.

rules.rule: frontmatter carries no keys outside {name, description}
rules.rationale: Only name and description are documented. An extra key may be ignored, may be rejected, or may be meaningful — unknown, so this warns rather than fails.
rules.remediation: Remove the extra key, or record an upload attempt that proves it is accepted.
rules.unverified: Which additional keys claude.ai Organization Skills accept is not in the claims table — verified by: an upload attempt with an extra key. Routed to plan section 8.

rules.rule: the SKILL.md body is at most 500 lines
rules.rationale: Documented performance guidance, not a hard limit — so this warns rather than fails. Overflow belongs in bundled resources, which cost nothing until accessed (S2).
rules.remediation: Move reference material into bundled files and link to them from the body.

rules.rule: every bundled file referenced from the body exists in the bundle
rules.rationale: A dead reference is a silent capability gap — the model follows the pointer and finds nothing. Objectively checkable and population-independent.
rules.remediation: Add the missing file to the bundle, or remove the reference.

rules.rule: no bundled file is referenced by an absolute path or a parent-directory traversal
rules.rationale: A path that escapes the bundle cannot resolve after upload, and a traversal is a packaging hazard.
rules.remediation: Reference bundled files relative to SKILL.md, with no leading slash and no parent traversal.

rules.rule: the archive contains exactly one SKILL.md
rules.rationale: Zero means nothing installs; more than one is ambiguous.
rules.remediation: Rebuild the archive from a single skill directory.

rules.rule: the archive root layout matches the settled convention
rules.rationale: UNSETTLED. S7 reads 'the ZIP root must be the skill folder itself, not a wrapper', which does not disambiguate `<name>/SKILL.md` from `SKILL.md` at depth 0 — the two planning panels read it in OPPOSITE directions and neither marked it unverified. This rule's tier is DERIVED from the evidence file, not hand-set: while that file records no settlement, the tier is warn. Promotion to fail is a data edit plus a fixture flip, never a code change.
rules.remediation: Both readings ship as fixtures (rootA-folder.zip, rootB-flat.zip). Upload each at Organization settings > Skills and record which installs, with the date, in reference/platform-constraints.md.

rules.rule: the archive contains no symlinks and no absolute or traversing member paths
rules.rationale: Archive-extraction safety; a traversing member is a packaging exploit shape regardless of intent.
rules.remediation: Rebuild the archive from a clean directory containing only regular files.

rules.rule: the archive does not contain the studio's own lint report
rules.rationale: A lint-clean stamp travelling inside the shipped bundle is a credibility transfer: it suppresses the only human review S10 leaves in place, because org-wide sharing has no approval step. The report is a local artifact, never a shipped one.
rules.remediation: Exclude the report from the archive. The packer does this by construction; this rule asserts that it did.

rules.rule: the description names no capability verb
rules.rationale: S3 requires the description to state what the skill does AND when to use it. A description with no verb states neither.
rules.remediation: Open with what it does: 'Extracts…', 'Generates…', 'Reviews…'.

rules.rationale: S5 prefers gerund (processing-pdfs) but explicitly ACCEPTS noun phrases and action forms. A style preference, never a defect.

rules.rule: the description uses first person outside quoted text
rules.rationale: S4 warns that inconsistent point-of-view causes discovery problems, since the description is injected into the system prompt.
rules.remediation: Rewrite in third person: 'Processes Excel files', not 'I can help you process Excel files'.

A naive version measured 0.3% (3/934) on this corpus and ALL THREE were false positives — every hit was 'I can' inside a quoted user utterance ('report I can show leadership'), i.e. it fired precisely on descriptions following best practice by quoting real user phrasing. With quoted spans excluded the rate is 0.0%. This is the run's clearest evidence that an unmeasured heuristic can be net-negative.

rules.rule: no literal credential of any shape appears in the description, the body, or any bundled file
rules.rationale: S20: the studio is a supply-chain surface. A provider-prefixed key is ground truth by construction (AKIA + 16 uppercase alnum IS an AWS key id), not a claim about author habits — which is why this may sit at FAIL where the entropy heuristic R1B may not.
rules.remediation: Remove the literal. If you are DOCUMENTING credential handling, use a placeholder (<TOKEN>, $API_KEY, YOUR_KEY) — those are recognised and do not fire.
rules.quarantine: fence + frame + handling instruction + a named reviewer in the EXTERNAL run record. Three of four is still FAIL.
rules.measured_note: 1/934 on the corpus: AWS's own documentation example key AWS's own documentation example key, inside a secrets-detection skill. Deliberately NOT special-cased to a pass. It is credential-SHAPED, and the unappealable scanner (S9) reads shapes; and an ends-with-EXAMPLE carve-out is the exact cleverness that lets a real key through when someone names a variable EXAMPLE. The quarantine path exists for precisely this case.

rules.rule: no unexplained high-entropy string (40+ chars, mixed case and digits, not a slug or a hex hash)
rules.rationale: An entropy heuristic cannot distinguish a secret from an opaque identifier, so it may not block. It is the backstop for a credential whose provider prefix R1 does not know.
rules.remediation: If it is a secret, remove it. If it is an opaque identifier, say what it is in a sentence beside it.

fire_rate.population: expert-authored Claude Code skills in this marketplace
fire_rate.note: 0/934 WITH A WORKING POSITIVE CONTROL — an opaque 44-char mixed-case token is caught (asserted in the battery). A 0.0% rate here means these authors do not paste secrets, NOT that the check is inert. Reaching 0 took two narrowings, both measured: admitting `/` in the charset made every long PATH match (2 of 3 hits), and an unbounded `(?=[^\s]*[A-Z])` lookahead was satisfied by an uppercase letter beyond the candidate, so an all-lowercase slug matched a rule requiring uppercase.

rules.rule: no global-posture override imperative (an instruction to set aside prior guidance, and its family)
rules.rationale: Provisioned org-wide, unreviewed if org sharing is on (S10), and injected into system prompts. An override imperative in that position is not a quotation.
rules.remediation: Paraphrase it FIRST: 'a message attempting to override the assistant's prior guidance' loses nothing operational and needs no reviewer. Only if the literal is genuinely required, use the quarantine path.
rules.quarantine: fence + frame + handling instruction + a named reviewer in the EXTERNAL run record. Three of four is still FAIL.
rules.measured_note: 2/934, both in skills ABOUT injection — one an imperative to set aside prior guidance, one a new-instructions header. The literals are PARAPHRASED here rather than quoted: dogfooding the studio on itself showed R2 firing on this very file, and paraphrase-first is the remedy this table's own refusals.md prescribes. It costs nothing — the note's content is the measurement, not the string. These are the quarantine cases, not false positives — the literal really is in the archive the classifier reads.

rules.rule: no covert channel: self-concealment from the user, or egress combined with a reference to conversation/user content
rules.rationale: The exfiltration half requires BOTH an egress imperative AND a conversation reference, because either alone is ordinary — a skill that POSTs to a ticketing API is normal, and one that discusses the transcript is normal. The conjunction is the covert channel.
rules.remediation: Make the call user-visible and scoped, and drop any instruction to withhold information from the user.
rules.quarantine: fence + frame + handling instruction + a named reviewer in the EXTERNAL run record. Three of four is still FAIL.
rules.measured_note: 0/934. The negative control that matters is asserted in the battery: a documented, scoped, user-visible external API call must NOT fire.

rules.rule: no tool-authority expansion (pipe-to-shell, install from an arbitrary URL)
rules.rationale: A bundle that instructs an install from an arbitrary URL hands the org's blast radius to whoever controls that URL.
rules.remediation: Pin the artifact and verify it. If you are documenting the anti-pattern, paraphrase it — 'piping a downloaded script straight into a shell' — which needs no reviewer.
rules.quarantine: fence + frame + handling instruction + a named reviewer in the EXTERNAL run record. Three of four is still FAIL.
rules.measured_note: 4/934, every one inside a skill DOCUMENTING the anti-pattern. This is gap-delta's 'a grep is satisfied by the thing being described', and it is why paraphrase-first is the documented first remedy rather than the quarantine path.

rules.rule: no persona override on a binding matter (an instruction to assume the identity of a lawyer, clinician or auditor)
rules.rationale: S10: there is no approval workflow, so a persona instruction reaches every member unreviewed. It is a judgement call whether a given persona overrides binding guidance, so it may not block.
rules.remediation: State the role as scope ('this skill covers contract review') rather than as an identity Claude should assume, and keep the escalation path.

rules.rule: the archive has exactly one distinct top-level path component
rules.rationale: Two top-level components means the unpacker has no unambiguous root to install. This is the wrapper-directory failure and its mirror, the loose-files failure.
rules.remediation: Rebuild from a single skill directory with `orgskill pack`.

rules.rule: SKILL.md is present and non-empty at the archive's root, and is valid UTF-8
rules.rationale: An archive whose SKILL.md is missing, empty or mis-encoded installs into nothing. Checked from the archive bytes, not the source tree.
rules.remediation: Rebuild the archive; if SKILL.md is non-empty on disk but empty here, the packer excluded or truncated it.

rules.rule: the archive contains no non-shippable entry (macOS Finder artifacts, VCS metadata, caches)
rules.rationale: The macOS Compress context-menu action emits __MACOSX/ sidecars and ._* resource forks the author never sees in Finder. An entry the author cannot see is an entry they cannot audit.
rules.remediation: Rebuild with `orgskill pack`, which excludes these by construction, rather than compressing the folder in Finder.

rules.rule: every relative link in the archived SKILL.md resolves to an entry present IN THE ARCHIVE
rules.rationale: S2 puts overflow in bundled files. The source tree can be complete while the archive is not — a dead bundled reference emits nothing at author time and fails only in production. Resolution is against the archive namelist, never the disk.
rules.remediation: Add the referenced file to the skill directory, or remove the link.

rules.rule: the archive extracts, and the EXTRACTED tree passes the linter
rules.rationale: Verification by attempt (gap-delta D4). A source tree that lints clean can still ship a broken bundle; case-collisions on a case-insensitive filesystem and encoding mangles also surface here rather than at upload. The source directory is not consulted.
rules.remediation: Read the underlying finding: it names the rule the extracted tree failed.

rules.rule: the SKILL.md filename uses the canonical casing
rules.rationale: WARN, not FAIL, because ANTHROPIC'S OWN SOURCES DISAGREE and none adjudicates: support article 12512198 writes lowercase skill.md throughout and never uses the uppercase form, while article 13119606 and the anthropics/skills repo write SKILL.md. Neither casing is demonstrably rejected by the platform. Hard-rejecting one of them would block an archive built by following Anthropic's own worked example — measured 2026-08-24: verify() did exactly that, reporting ZP01 'contains 0 SKILL.md entries' on an otherwise valid bundle.
rules.remediation: Rename to SKILL.md — it matches the org-facing article and Anthropic's repo. This is a preference, not a known requirement; nothing states an upload fails on the other casing.
rules.casing_note: Resolution needs an upload attempt, which is also what would settle ZP02. Recorded in reference/platform-constraints.md under the research block's unresolved side-issues.

id_note: Rule ids are this implementation's, and they DEVIATE from plan-A's draft numbering in two places: plan-A used FM06 for reserved-words and FM10 for extra-frontmatter-keys, which this table had already assigned to description-present and body-present before those rules were specified. Renumbering committed ids is churn with no benefit, so the new rules take FM11/FM12 and this note records the mapping. ZP ids deviate from the plan's draft numbering for the same reason: ZP01-ZP04 were committed in Phase 0 before the archive checks were specified, so the new checks take ZP05-ZP09 rather than renumbering committed ids. Mapping — plan ZP01 (one top-level component) = ZP05; plan ZP03 (SKILL.md present/non-empty) = ZP06; plan ZP04 (Finder artifacts) = ZP07; plan ZP05+ZP06 (traversal, symlinks) = the committed combined ZP03, which emits a distinguishing message per shape; plan ZP07 (links resolve in-archive) = ZP08; plan ZP08 (extract and re-lint) = ZP09. This table's ZP01 (exactly one SKILL.md) and ZP04 (the report must not travel) have no plan counterpart and are additional.
refusal_note: R1-R4 are hard refusals with NO override flag, env var or config key. Their only path is quarantine: fence + frame + handling instruction + A NAMED HUMAN REVIEWER RECORDED IN THE EXTERNAL RUN RECORD. The fourth condition is the one the author cannot supply alone — plan-A's three-part incantation is authored entirely by whoever wrote the adversarial string, which is self-attestation with extra steps, i.e. a --force spelled out in the documentation. A reviewer line inside SKILL.md clears nothing. An adversarial literal in the frontmatter DESCRIPTION has no quarantine path at all: it is injected verbatim into every member's system prompt. ⛔ THIS TABLE PARAPHRASES EVERY ADVERSARIAL LITERAL IT DESCRIBES. Dogfooding the studio on its own directory showed R1/R2/R5 firing on this file's rule text and measured_note fields — the studio would have refused to pack itself, on the exact defect its own refusals.md tells authors to fix by paraphrasing. Nothing operational was lost: a rule's content is the constraint and the measurement, never the string. Do not restore the literals for 'clarity'.
